exercises.name: Plantar fasciitis: high-load heel raise
exercises.description:
Every other day for about three months. Roll up a towel and put it under your toes so they are held bent upward — that is what loads the plantar fascia rather than only the calf. Stand with the ball of the foot on the edge of a step and rise on the painful leg alone: three seconds up, two seconds held at the top, three seconds down.

Twelve repetitions, three sets, a minute between sets. Use both legs to rise at first if one is too painful, and add load as it gets easier — a rucksack with books — moving to 10 repetitions × 4 sets, then 8 × 5, so the last repetition of every set is always hard. That progression is the point: in the trial this protocol beat plantar-specific stretching on pain and function at three months.

Pain during the exercise up to about 5 out of 10 that settles by the next morning is acceptable. Give it three months before judging it. Not medical advice.

catalog.source: Rathleff et al., High-load strength training improves outcome in patients with plantar fasciitis, Scand J Med Sci Sports 2015;25(3):e292-300
